target.title: feat(mcp): open App views from channel replies
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

MCP App tool results already render inline in Control UI, but channel turns lose that interactive view. Telegram, Slack, Discord, and text-only transports preserve the assistant text yet provide no way to open the latest successful App view.

## Why This Change Was Made

This carries only the latest successful view identity through the agent result, then materializes one portable `web-app` presentation action after the final visible reply has been normalized. The Gateway mints the existing standalone-view ticket at that last moment, bounds it to the live view lease, and uses one lifecycle-owned HTTPS origin prepared by Tailscale Serve or Funnel. Channel adapters retain transport ownership; prerequisite #111116 keeps Telegram's native `web_app` button DM-only and falls back to the portable HTTPS action elsewhere.

Control UI remains unchanged and receives no duplicate action. Missing origin, capacity, lease, transport support, or an expired view leaves the original reply text intact. The action contains only a fixed label and opaque URL; App HTML, input/result data, session identity, view metadata, and bearer credentials are not serialized into channel payloads.

## User Impact

Users can open the latest MCP App from the final assistant reply in Telegram DMs, Slack, and Discord. Other transports keep an understandable text-and-link fallback. Tailscale Serve links remain tailnet-only; Funnel links are internet-reachable. Existing reply text and Control UI behavior are preserved.

## Owner Approval

Jason explicitly approved this PR's internet-reachable Funnel bearer capability and the separate trusted proof-harness work needed to exercise it. The capability remains short-lived, opaque, bounded by the live view lease, and free of App/session/result metadata. Approval is also recorded in [the PR discussion](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/111211#issuecomment-5014566456). Trusted harness prerequisite #111238 landed separately.

## Evidence

- The refreshed feature matrix passed 431 focused assertions across agent, Gateway, harness, Telegram, Slack, and Discord shards on `cc0f60987ef868b79fdb2a96c081a091eff0df1e`: [run 29676736902](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29676736902).
- After the final unrelated main merge, exact PR head `eafd7c236dcb46f0f1662910cc77a8cd99467da5` passed the incoming sidebar tests, authenticated MCP App browser conformance, and the full private-QA build/package/export/performance gates: [run 29676869715](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29676869715).
- Fresh whole-branch autoreview on the exact pushed head reported no actionable findings (0.87 confidence).
- Exact-head GitHub CI is green.
- The strict exact-head Telegram workflow validated and built both refs but failed closed before any session launched: [run 29677216366](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29677216366). The Crabbox coordinator's Tailscale OAuth token returned HTTP 401 for both Hetzner and AWS Tailscale-enabled desktop lease attempts. The redacted manifest records `comparison.pass: false` with no artifacts. Credential-owner rotation is required before native button receipt/open, official-SDK fixture render, app-only tool result, resource read, and same-button expiry can be proven. This PR must not merge until that proof passes.

AI-assisted: yes. I understand and reviewed the full owner/caller/callee/channel surface and addressed the accepted autoreview finding before opening this PR.
